subject: Call on the Federal Government to end the free ride for fossil fuels! - Climate Council
posts:
Urging the federal government to stop subsidizing polluting energy.
Evidence: Record profits, climate disaster costs, public burden
#Aletheia #Climate

Ending fossil fuel subsidies protects taxpayers and accelerates clean energy.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

Public pressure pushes back against entrenched fossil fuel interests.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.7, +0.8) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Awakening.
Community advocacy challenges entrenched corporate extraction structures.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.2, z: 0)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Climate Council Advocacy: PASS (+0.8, +0.9) — Clear public interest campaign.
- Fossil Fuel Subsidy System: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Externalizes environmental costs.
The Climate Council's campaign highlights how ordinary citizens absorb the mounting financial tolls of extreme weather while fossil fuel giants retain massive subsidies.

The Bright Side:
Grassroots mobilization directly challenges corporate welfare structures.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing political lobbying power (WHO) with neutral market pricing (WHAT).

Social Physics Analysis:
The Climate Council counters a Smart Selfish Maneuver where fossil fuel incumbents externalize ecological destruction while pocketing public subsidies.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map advocacy against systemic extraction, it charts a course toward structural transparency and reform. Δ(p·t + n) > 0.

The Unavoidable Truth: Fossil fuel externalities are paid by taxpayers through disaster relief and health costs.

The Unavoidable Lie: Subsidies reflect a free-market equilibrium.

Alethekanon:
Challenging corporate subsidies exposes the hidden state support underpinning fossil fuel extraction.🌐

Awwthekanon:
It takes courage to speak up for communities bearing the hidden costs of climate damage, reminding us that true progress honors both people and our shared home.

Brothekanon:
Feels like common sense: if corporations make record profits, they shouldn't need government handouts while everyone else pays for climate cleanups.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act." Proverbs 3:27 PASS
Withholding corporate welfare corrects a fundamental injustice against everyday taxpayers.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Call on the Federal Government to end the free ride for fossil fuels! - Climate Council

Actual Article Body:
Growing a bigger, cleaner energy grid.

How we make things matters.

Cleaner, cheaper and better transport choices.

Take Action

/

Climate Politics

Meanwhile, the rest of us are left footing the bill for the climate damage.

Higher insurance premiums, spiralling costs for imported fuel, and billions in disaster recovery from worsening fires, floods and heatwaves are among the costs we pay for fossil fuel pollution, and they hit harder every year.

But while everyday Australians tighten their belts, highly polluting coal, oil and gas corporations are raking in record profits and pocketing billions in government subsidies, leaving everyday Australians to pick up the tab for the climate damage.

It’s time for that to change. Right now, decisions are being made that will determine whether fossil fuel corporations keep getting a free ride at our expense, or whether they are held to account.

This is the moment to make our voices heard.

That means:

Stated Claim / Post Context:
TEMA to upgrade statewide emergency warnings with $10.6M federal grant

Tennessee was awarded $10.6 million through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Fiscal Year 2026 to support strengthening statewide emergency warning systems.

Actual Article Body:
What This Story Is About

Why It Matters

What Happens Next

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Tennessee was awarded $10.6 million through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Fiscal Year 2026 to support strengthening statewide emergency warning systems.

The following approved projects will establish “additional alert and warning pathways” across Tennessee:

The Tennessee Emergency Management Authority said the projects will help reduce reliance on communication methods and improve Tennessee’s ability to reach residents, visitors, facilities and public safety partners during severe weather, wildfires, hazardous materials incidents, infrastructure failures and other emergencies.

‘This is new to me’ — What a former federal judge says LDS President Dallin Oaks taught him about the Constitution
